name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
title: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd - 540699 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 revenue flat on smartphone demand and memory-cost headwinds; management guides FY27 non-Vivo volumes flat with 12-15% price-led mobile revenue growth, PLI roll-off trims margins ~50-70bps, and display/camera backward integration is the margin lever for FY27-28.

summary.headline: Dixon Q4 FY26 revenue flat at INR10,520 crore; FY26 revenue up 26% to INR48,893 crore, with FY27 guided to INR56,000 crore ex-Vivo.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was flat, with management citing geopolitical concerns, softer consumer demand, brand inventory rationalisation and memory-chip cost inflation in smartphones and IT hardware. Q4 EBITDA excluding exceptional gain was INR418 crore and PAT after minority interest was INR192 crore. For the full year, revenue rose 26% to INR48,893 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR845 crore, excluding exceptional gain. Management guided FY27 to about INR56,000 crore excluding Vivo, with mobile volumes flat and smartphone selling prices up 12-15%, and said the PLI roll-off will compress margins this year.

segments.name: Mobile and other EMS
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR9,485 crore and operating profit INR337 crore. Management expects high-double-digit QoQ volume growth and 12-15% selling price growth, with exports from Ismartu starting mid-Q2.

segments.name: Telecom and networking
segments.commentary: Revenue grew from INR3,600 crore to INR5,000 crore in FY26, with a target of INR7,500-8,000 crore in FY27 and high-double-digit growth guided. Microwave radio exports planned this fiscal.

segments.name: IT hardware
segments.commentary: Management expects revenue above INR4,000 crore in FY27, about 3x FY26. Chennai unit is in stabilised mass production of laptops and all-in-ones, and SSD manufacturing at the Inventec JV starts in Q2.

segments.name: Home appliances
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR329 crore and operating profit INR31 crore. Semi-auto washing machines in 16 and 18 kg started; Tirupati adds 0.3 million units to the 0.6 million capacity.

segments.name: Lighting (Signify JV)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR800-850 crore; FY27 target about INR1,700 crore (2x). Export orders from a US chain and a European retail chain start in Q2, outside the AOP.

segments.name: Consumer electronics (LED TV and refrigerators)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR697 crore and operating profit INR40 crore. Demand slowed temporarily; refrigerator demand was hit by the transition to revised PE norms. A 375,000 sq ft expansion is planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR56,000 crore excluding Vivo, with mobile volumes flat and growth of about 15-17% without Vivo.
FY27 smartphone volumes ex-Vivo expected to be similar to FY26 (about 32-33 million including exports, management said), with exports potentially additive.
FY27 margin under pressure from PLI roll-off, with 40-50 bps expansion expected once the component play is fully deployed; absolute profit guided to rise.
Industrial/specialty EMS: at least a couple of inorganic opportunities expected to close in FY27, potentially INR3,000-4,000 crore in scale at significantly higher margins; not budgeted.

Display JV (74:26 with HKC): trials from Q3 FY27 and commercial production from Q4 FY27; mobile capacity to go from 24 million to 50-55 million over two years, with revenue of INR5,500-6,000 crore at mid-teens margin at 80-90% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Q Tech camera module capacity to rise from 70 million to 180-190 million units over 15-18 months; revenue target about INR2,500 crore vs about INR1,700 crore annualised.
Noida 1 million sq ft facility for anchor customers nearing completion, with operations expected from Q2 FY27.
Longcheer JV 400,000 sq ft facility expected to start operations by Q3 FY27.
FY26 capex about INR1,058 crore; FY27 capex expected to be in a similar range, focused on display, IT hardware and camera modules. Cash accruals deemed adequate.
Display JV: building complete and machinery being installed; Phase 1 capacity is 24 million mobile displays and 2.4 million automotive/IT displays annually.
demand_pricing: Memory-chip inflation and AI-led demand are raising smartphone BoM costs, leading to cautious brand procurement and softer demand; management says supply is not constrained and there is no production impact.

Smartphone selling prices are expected to rise 12-15%, so revenue growth should exceed volume growth. Under the per-unit conversion model, margin percentages will look lower optically while absolute per-unit profit holds.
Vivo: management says approval is very close; annualised volume of about 20-22 million units could be added on top of the existing base. Vivo sold about 35 million units last year.
FY26 smartphone exports were about 4-4.5 million units (about INR5,375 crore by value per the call); feature phone exports to Africa via Ismartu and HMD smartphones are planned.
PLI-related margin impact previously guided at 50-70 bps is confirmed as the full effect, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI income booked and outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Total PLI income across the four schemes is about INR360 crore gross, with INR960 crore passed through (net figure not clearly stated). Receivable is about INR1,380 crore across the four schemes, of which about INR1,100 crore is PLI receivable and INR730 crore payable. The overflow from the scheme's underperformance mechanism is pending with the government.

qa_highlights.question: How does memory-driven ASP inflation affect revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is a function of BoM plus conversion charge, so BoM inflation lifts revenue. Dixon earns a per-unit EBITDA set by model complexity, so per-unit profit holds while percentage margin looks lower.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of the FY27 volume ramp and is H2-weighted?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume was about 5.6 million. Management guided high-double-digit QoQ growth, Q2 is seasonally strongest, and exports start from Q2; excluding Vivo volumes are seen as similar year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for display ramp and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobile display trials and commercial production start Q4 FY27; at 80-90% utilisation, revenue is INR5,500-6,000 crore at double-digit margin, mid-teens per management. FY28 is expected to be a partial ramp.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex and currency/commodity risk look?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is similar in size, focused on display, IT hardware and camera modules. EMS is a pure pass-through with no currency risk; ODM appliances pass cost increases to customers with a lag of a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the display fab deprioritised and how big is industrial EMS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a standalone display fab is lower priority. Specialty EMS could be INR3,000-4,000 crore in scale at higher margins, with no PLI dependence.

risks_watch: Vivo government approval timing, which is a major swing factor for FY27 volumes and revenue.
Memory-chip and component inflation, with possible demand softness and brand inventory cautiousness in smartphones and IT hardware.
Margin pressure from PLI roll-off until backward integration (camera modules H2 FY27, display FY27-28) takes effect.
Pending PLI overflow receivable of about INR1,380 crore across four schemes, and the PLI-related payable of about INR730 crore.
Execution risk on the display JV ramp, IT hardware (3x growth target), industrial EMS M&A, and the Inventec JV SSD line.
Refrigerator demand after the PE norm transition and the temporary slowdown in LED TVs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term pipeline and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term demand, with memory-cost-driven softness acknowledged. Management was evasive on Vivo timing ("very close") and declined to split segment numbers or give display FY27 numbers.
key_quotes: Q4 revenues remained flat due to geopolitical concerns, softer consumer demand, inventory rationalization by brands, elevated input costs, majorly impacting the smartphone and IT hardware segment.
So yes, possibly, I should have tried it 2 years back.
So the margins may optically can be lower, but the revenue-wise, there will be upside on that.
